1. Overview
ONDC API contract maps various use cases to APIs and ensures interoperability as follows:
* by defining the set of attributes that need to be exchanged between the BNP & SNP, to initiate & complete a transaction;
* clearly defining the single source of truth for each attribute key and thereby establishing mutability & immutability of these keys on behalf of NPs at each end of the transaction;
This document is structured as follows:
* different pre-order & post-order APIs, for the baseline requirements, along with sample json payload;
* transaction flows for different "enhanced" use cases;
* expected behaviour of APIs for different use cases;
All attributes, defined in this API contract, are mandatory, unless explicitly mentioned otherwise. Additionally, NPs may send optional attributes as per the swagger spec here. Participants may validate the request & response payloads, based on attributes as defined, and respond appropriately;
All participants are required to ensure full compliance with this API contract on the live ONDC network.
________________
2. Construct of APIs & transaction trail
1. All APIs follow the same construct and include:
* Context - includes transaction_id, message_id and other attribute keys that identify the source & destination of the message being sent through the API request or response;
* Message - identifies the content of the message e.g. the search intent, catalog details, order details, etc.;
2. All APIs are asynchronous, i.e.:
* request is sent from sender to recipient;
* recipient acknowledges the request by sending an "ACK" (or "NACK" if they cannot validate the request);
* recipient sends response through the callback for the corresponding request API e.g. /on_search callback for /search request;
* recipient of callback (could be the original sender) acknowledges the response by sending an "ACK" (or "NACK" if they cannot validate the request);
3. Every request & response pair is identified by a transaction_id + unique message_id & the sender of a request is able to correlate the response to the request using the above;
4. Error block can be sent in sync (in response to request) or async (along with callback) mode and should have the following attribute keys: error.type, error.code (mapped to standard error codes defined here);
5. Transaction trail for a buyer is maintained through a unique transaction_id for the pre-order stage, i.e. /search, /select, /init, /confirm and post-order stage ie. /status, /cancel, /update, /track. However, considering that most buyer apps cache catalogs that are reused by multiple buyer apps, for providing a good buyer experience, a unique transaction_id is maintained for /select, /init & /confirm.
6. Unique id for an order on a network will be identified by the transaction_id & order id;
7. If a stale request or response is received, i.e. with timestamp earlier than similar request or response (identified by the transaction_id + message_id) that has already been processed, the recipient can send "NACK" with the error code "20002" (BNP) and "30022" (SNP);
8. Buyer apps with live search functionality can use the same transaction_id across the entire pre-order stage;
9. Swagger link is here;
________________
   3. Signing & Verification of requests & responses
   1. Key pairs, for signing & encryption, can be generated using any standard library e.g. libsodium, Bouncy Castle, etc.
   2. Creating key pairs
   * create key pairs, for signing (ed25519) & encryption (X25519);
   * update base64 encoded public keys in registry;
   * utility to generate signing key pairs and test signing & verification is here;
   3. Auth Header Signing
   * generate UTF-8 byte array from json payload;
   * generate Blake2b hash from UTF-8 byte array;
   * create base64 encoding of Blake2b hash, this becomes the digest for signing;
   * sign the request, using your private signing key, and add the signature to the request authorization header, following steps documented here;
   4. Auth Header Verification
   * extract the digest from the encoded signature in the request;
   * get the signing_public_key from registry using lookup (by using the ukId in the authorization header);
   * create (UTF-8) byte array from the raw payload and generate Blake2b hash;
   * compare generated Blake2b hash with the decoded digest from the signature in the request;
   * in case of failure to verify, HTTP error 401 should be thrown;
Registry lookup
   1. There are 2 possible participant types, for each domain, in the ONDC registry:
   * Buyer NP
   * Seller NP


        Seller NP could be either ISN (Inventory Seller Node) or MSN (Marketplace Seller Node or Aggregator)
   2. Each participant type, defined above, will have an entry in the registry for their entity. Every participant on the ONDC registry will have one or more entries in the registry, with unique identifier ("ukid") for each such entry;
   3. All requests & responses have to be signed by the sender and verified by the receiver. If any request fails verification, it should be rejected (NACK’d) with http 401 error code;
   4. The identity of the sender of a request is sent, through the auth header, as follows:
keyId="{subscriber_id}|{unique_key_id}|{algorithm}"
   5. BNP & SNP will use their private key for signing, for which the corresponding public key will be in the registry, for their "ukid";
   6. Verification of requests using registry lookup uses this API spec. Participants can either use the registry lookup endpoints from here or cache the registry locally (with refresh at regular intervals) for a local lookup;
   7. Following options are available:
   * /v2.0/lookup
request:
    {
        "subscriber_id":"bnp.com",
        "domain[1]":"ONDC:RET10",
        "ukId":"UKID1",
        "country[2]":"IND",
        "city[3]":"std:080",
        "type[4]":"BPP"
    }


/v2.0/lookup supports secure access using Authorization headers. Steps to create Authorization header is mentioned in 3.c above. 


Sample Curl: 


curl --location 'https://prod.registry.ondc.org/v2.0/lookup' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Signature keyId="example-bap.com|bap1234|ed25519", algorithm="ed25519", created="<timestamp>", expires="<timestamp>", headers="(created)(expires)digest", signature="<signature>"' \
--data '{
  "subscriber_id":"bnp.com",
  "ukId":"UKID1"
}'


response:
(will be an array with 1 or more objects, depending on whether the entity, identified by the subscriber_id, has registered as different participants in a domain, e.g. BNP, SNP)
[
    {
        "subscriber_id":"bnp.com",
        "status":"SUBSCRIBED",
        "ukId":"UKID1",
        "subscriber_url":"https://bnp.com/ondc",
        "country":"IND",
        "domain":"ONDC:RET10",
        "valid_from":"2023-06-03T06:00:00.000Z",
        "valid_until":"2027-06-02T06:00:00.000Z",
        "type":"BPP",
        "signing_public_key": "<ed25519_signing_public_key>",
        "encr_public_key": "<x25519_encryption_public_key>",
        "created":"2023-06-03T06:00:00.000Z",
        "updated":"2023-06-03T06:00:00.000Z",
        "br_id":"<br_id>",
        "city":"std:080"
    }
]

________________
   4. Version compatibility
   1. For all new features enabled from 1.2.5:
   1. List of all "baseline" & "enhanced" features is here;
   2. Transaction flow for new features, with corresponding feature id, is here;
   3. BNPs & SNPs may prioritize & enable one or more features as per their business requirements;
   4. BNP & SNP will publish the list of features enabled for mutual feature discovery;
   5. Context.version, for the corresponding APIs, will be set to "1.2.5";
   2. Version 1.2.5 will be considered an update to version 1.2.0 & hence will be fully backward compatible with version 1.2.0 (but not with 1.1.0):
   1. Each new feature will be incrementally layered on the base version 1.2.0;
   2. "1.2.5" version of these APIs will be fully backward compatible with "1.2.0" version of the same APIs:
   * BNP sends 1.2.0 API request => some SNPs may send 1.2.0 response, other SNPs may send 1.2.5 response;
   * BNP sends 1.2.5 API request => some SNPs may send 1.2.0 response, other SNPs may send 1.2.5 response;
   * BNP sending 1.2.5 request must also include the list of features supported;
   * SNP supporting 1.2.5 features may enable business workflows for supported features based on mutual feature discovery;
   3. NPs may have version check enabled for "1.2.*";
Full catalog refresh
   * Search request is always broadcast through the gateway so that all NPs who have registered for the specific domain, in the search request, are notified;
   * Full catalog response will be sent directly from the SNPs to the BNP, from which the search request was received through the gateway;
   * The SNP should send the full catalog response in GZIP-compressed format to support large payloads over the APIs. The callback response must include the HTTP header Content-Encoding: gzip to indicate compression;
/search (by city)
   * /search will be used to communicate the intent for a full (or incremental) catalog refresh;
   * BNP can optionally refresh catalogs for a city by sub-category, e.g. for Grocery (ONDC:RET10), catalog can be refreshed separately for each sub-category:
   * e.g. for "Bakery, Cakes & Dairy", Context.domain="ONDC:RET10", category.id = "Bakery, Cakes & Dairy";
   * distributed search i.e. by category will also allow differential buyer finder fee for different sub-categories in a domain;
   * however, this will not be possible for categories, such as F&B, where no such sub-categories are defined;
   * Buyer NP (BNP) will also publish the static terms for transaction level contract through this API;
{
  "context":

________________
/on_search
   * Full catalog refresh includes the complete catalog, per provider, for SNP at a point in time (as identified by Context.timestamp). If BNP is caching the catalog, the list of items for a provider will be overwritten with the list of items in the catalog refresh, i.e. existing items in the BNP cache which aren’t in the catalog refresh will be disabled;
   * However, since SNPs may send separate catalog responses per provider (i.e. pagination by provider), it is possible that a catalog response for a provider may not be received by the BNP. Hence, provider(s) must be explicitly disabled, through the incremental refresh, and cannot be disabled if a response isn’t received in the catalog response;
   * Includes the following:
   * Customizations & Variants
   * Customizations may be used to create make-to-order products (e.g. F&B), by defining the base product and the mandatory & optional customizations for the product;
   * Customizations will be enabled using customization groups and individual customizations:
   * Individual customizations are similar to SKU items (with price, inventory, veg/non-veg attributes);
   * Customizations can also be used to send special instructions e.g. for:
   * Food preparation ("less spicy", "less salt", etc.);
   * Packaging related instructions (card for "Happy Birthday", etc.);
   * Variants may be used by BNPs to group multiple items for display;
   * Even though the examples here show customizations & variants for specific categories, it can be used for other categories such as electronics, fashion, grocery, pharma, home & kitchen, etc.;
   * Custom Menu
   * Custom Menu may be used to define a provider-level menu, for BNP rendering. Even though the examples below show custom menus for F&B, it can be used for other categories such as electronics, fashion, grocery, etc.;
   * Custom menu structure is hierarchical and can include multiple levels;
   * Custom menu will have display sequence at each of the levels;
   * Item can be assigned to multiple menu items, with ranking for display within the custom menu;
   * The menu items will have an unique display sequence, for parent & child menu items;
   * Separate UOM & quantity for item
   * Provider level features
   * Enabling store (i.e. location), which may have been disabled in incremental catalog refresh;
   * Provider level fulfillment options, e.g. for delivery, self-pickup and the corresponding timings (for hyperlocal categories only);
   * Enhanced store timings;
   * Rating at Provider/Item level
   * Rating may be used to provide aggregate user rating for provider/item(s) - as maintained by SNP;
   * Rating can be provided on a scale of 1 to 5 with a precision of up to one decimal place;


________________
Catalog (F&B)
F&B catalog includes the following:
   * Base (SKU) items with item id e.g. "Farmhouse Pizza";
   * 1 or more customization groups defined for the provider, along with configurations (id, name, min / max, input type, sequence for display), e.g. "Crust", "Size";
   * 1 or more customizations - each customization is similar to base item and each customization may be assigned to 1 or more customization group, e.g. "Small", "Medium", "Large" may be customizations assigned to customization group "Size";
   * Customizations for the base item as follows:
   * base (SKU) item may be customized using 1 or more customization groups;
   * if any of the mandatory customizations aren’t defined (i.e. definition for customization group with min > 0 is not found or invalid or no customizations mapped to this customization group), BNP may consider the base item as invalid & disable accordingly;
   * configurations (min / max, sequence for display) may be overridden at item level. If not overridden, configurations will be inherited from the customization group definition;
   * Sample payload is below and includes every construct both required & optional for F&B. Detailed examples, for specific use-cases are below;

2. F&B (Mexican Patty Sandwich)
Variant (1 option) *
	Choice of bread (1 option) *
	Choice of preparation
	Choose Add Ons (up to 1 option)
	Choose Veggies (up to 1 option)
	Choose Sauces (up to 1 option)
	Choose Offers (up to 1 option)
	Mexican Bean Patty 15cm [6 inches]
(customization - C1, customization group - CG1, nested customization groups - CG2, CG3, CG4, CG6, CG7, CG8)
	Multigrain Honey Oats
(customization - C3, customization group - CG2)
Parmesan Oregano;
(customization - C4, customization group - CG2)
	Plain bread
(customization - C5, customization group - CG3)
Toasted bread;
(customization - C6, customization croup - CG3)
	Extra Cheese Slice (₹30)
(customization - C7, customization group - CG4)
	Lettuce
(customization - C9, customization group - CG6)
	Eggless Mayo
(customization - C9, customization group - CG7)
	Dark Chunk Choc Cookies (₹99)
(customization - C10, customization group - CG8)
	Make Cheese Pull Mexican Patty 30cm (₹270)
(customization - C2, customization group - CG1, nested customization groups - CG2, CG5, CG7, CG8)
	N/A
	Extra Mexican Bean Patty Footlong (₹120)
(customization - C8, customization group - CG5)
	N/A
	In this example:
   * Base price is ₹229 and all prices shown in the table above are incremental to the base price;
   * Mandatory customizations - variant, choice of bread;
   * Optional customizations - choice of preparation, add ons, veggies, sauces, offers;
   * 1 item (SKU) will be defined for the product and all customizations defined as related items (with inventory, price, veg/non-veg attributes) and customization groups;
   * Customization & Customization groups mapped above & defined in the payload below;

3. F&B - (Veg & Non-Veg Pizza Combo)
Choice of Crust (any 1 option)
	First Veg Half (any 1 option)
	Second Non-Veg Half (any 1 option)
	Pan Tossed
(customization - C1, customization group - CG1, nested customization group - CG2, CG3)
Cheese Blast (₹99)
(customization - C2, customization group - CG1, nested customization group - CG2, CG3)
Chicken Cheese Blast (₹129)
(customization - C3, customization group - CG1, nested customization group - CG2, CG3)
	Double Cheese Margherita
(customization - C4, customization group - CG2)
Paneer Tikka (₹50)
(customization - C5, customization group - CG2)
Farmer’s Market
(customization - C6, customization group - CG2)
Spicy Mexicano (₹50)
(customization - C7, customization group - CG2)
	Chicken Smokey Joe
(customization - C8, customization group - CG3)
Peri Peri Chicken (₹40)
(customization - C9, customization group - CG3)
BBQ Chicken (₹40)
(customization - C10, customization group - CG3)
	In this example:
   * Base price is ₹400 and all prices shown in the table above are incremental to the base price;
   * Mandatory customizations - choice of crust, first veg half, second non-veg half;
   * 1 item (SKU) will be defined for the product and all customizations defined as related items (with inventory, price, veg/non-veg attributes) linked to customization groups;
   * Customization & Customization groups mapped above & defined in the payload below;

Incremental catalog refresh
   * Incremental refresh is necessary for BNPs that cache catalogs and have to reflect changes since the last full catalog refresh;
   * Incremental refresh will include:
   * item(s) changes - entire item record to be sent when there are delta changes since the last full catalog snapshot;
   * store temporarily closed for online orders;
   * store (i.e. provider location) disabling;
   * provider / merchant disabling;
   * Incremental refresh will not include:
   * disabling & enabling of customization groups, custom menu, variants will be through the full catalog refresh;
   * new provider(s) / location(s);
   * Every BNP that wants to consume incremental catalog changes should send a /search request through the gateway, with following params:
   * mode - "start", "stop";
   * start_time - start time for incremental refresh;
   * end_time - end time for incremental refresh;
   * Following scenarios are possible:
   * BNP requests 1-time incremental refresh:
   * start_time < Context.timestamp, end_time <= Context.timestamp, end_time > start_time
   * means BNP pulls incremental updates from start_time to end_time in a single solicited response;
   * response will have the same transaction_id & message_id as the request;
   * BNP requests regular incremental refresh until stopped:
   * mode="start", start_time <= Context.timestamp (means SNP pushes incremental updates from start_time at a frequency range of 1-30 mins). If no start_time provided, it defaults to Context.timestamp;
   * SNP should aggregate and push updates, at the same time, to all BNPs that have requested for incremental refresh;
   * each response will have the same transaction_id but different message_id;
   * if there are no incremental catalog updates, SNP should not send empty catalog;
   * Buyer NP requests stopping of incremental refresh:
   * mode="stop";
   * transaction_id for stop incremental search request should be same as start incremental search request;
   * All the above scenarios are mandatory for all NPs;
   * At any point of time, BNP may have only 1 open incremental search request (i.e. 1-time or regular):
   * Accordingly, BNP needs to stop the current incremental search request before initiating a new incremental search request:
   * To handle race condition where BNP receives full & incremental refresh at the same time:
   * to enable BNP to distinguish between full vs incremental catalog response, a custom response header should be used by SNPs:
   * "X-ONDC-Search-Response:inc" - for incremental response;
   * "X-ONDC-Search-Response:full" - for full response;
   * since incremental catalog changes are sent directly to BNP, the auth header will only have the signature of SNP (and not include the gateway signature in x-gateway-authorization);
   * versioning is enabled for both types of refresh:
   * full refresh will have a timestamp at the provider & location level and indicates when the snapshot was generated;
   * incremental refresh will have a timestamp at provider / location / item level and indicates the time of the event;
   * in case BNP receives full & incremental refresh at the same time, either of these approaches for processing is feasible:
   * BNP can process the full refresh and then initiate incremental refresh e.g. if full refresh at 8AM was ingested between 8-9AM, BNP can stop the incremental refresh before initiating the full refresh or choose to ignore all incremental refresh within this duration of catalog ingestion. After processing the full refresh, BNP can initiate incremental refresh based on the timestamp in full refresh;
   * BNP can process full & incremental refresh in sequence and use the timestamp to decide which incremental refresh updates to persist;
   * To handle error conditions:
   * BNP not responding or responding with a NACK:
   * SNP should push catalog updates in multiple incremental refresh until ACK is received from all BNPs[c][d]. Response format for NACK is here;
   * BNP that didn’t request for incremental catalog changes should respond with NACK for all incremental catalog changes received;
   * In the sync ACK/NACK response to incremental catalog refresh, BNP can communicate whether the refresh was successfully ingested or not and the error codes & message format are defined here;

3. Store reopening
   * following states can be passed for a store in the catalog refresh:
   * open - open an already enabled store:
   * using full / incremental catalog refresh;
   * using time.label="open", time.timestamp = event timestamp;
   * store will be shown as open after BNP processes the incremental refresh;
   * after the store reopens, it will default to the normal store timings;
   * if used for disabled store, BNP may NACK with error code 20004;
   * close - close an already enabled store:
   * using full / incremental catalog refresh;
   * using time.label="close", time.timestamp = event timestamp, time.range.start = start datetime for closure, time.range.end is optional;
   * if time.range.end is not passed, the store will remain closed until it is marked as open in a subsequent catalog refresh (incremental or full);
   * any subsequent incremental catalog refresh that happens, when the store remains closed, may have updates for the items for that store. BNP should process this so that the updated items are visible when the store reopens;
   * any subsequent full catalog refresh that happens, when the store remains closed, will have the store marked as closed, along with the other details that are a part of the full catalog;
   * enable - for activation of store by BNP or for updating other information including serviceability, items, store timing, etc:
   * using full catalog refresh (for now);
   * using time.label="enable", time.timestamp = event timestamp;
   * store timings using provider.timing;
   * disable - for soft-delete of store by BNP:
   * using full / incremental catalog refresh;
   * using time.label="disable", time.timestamp = event timestamp;

/on_search sync response (ACK, NACK)
In the sync response to incremental catalog refresh /on_search, the BNP can send ACK or NACK:
   * ACK means refresh was successfully ingested;
   * NACK means refresh couldn’t be ingested and could happen because the incremental refresh being shared for specific provider(s) / location(s) / item(s) are not found on the BNP cache or for other reasons. BNP should use these error codes / message in the NACK response:
   * provider not found - error code 20003, error message should have provider id delimited by comma, e.g. "[{provider_id:P1},{provider_id:P2},{provider_id:P3}]" (means provider ids P1, P2, P3 are not found);
   * provider location not found - error code 20004, error message should have provider & location ids delimited by comma, e.g. "[{provider_id:P1,location_id:L1}, {provider_id:P2,location_id:L2}]" (means location id L1 for provider id P1, location id L2 for provider id P2 are not found);
   * item not found - error code 20005, error message should have provider & item ids delimited by comma, e.g. "[{provider_id:P1,item_id:I1}, {provider_id:P2,item_id:I2}]" (means item id I1 for provider id P1, item id I2 for provider id P2 are not found);[g][h]
   * for a combination of the above errors, error codes should be delimited by comma and above error messages combined in stringified json, e.g. if the following not found:
   * provider location L3 for provider P1
   * item id I3 for provider P2
   * error code - "20004,20005" and error message - "[{provider_id:P1,location_id:L3}, {provider_id:P2,item_id:I3}]"
   * for all other cases, error code 20000, error message will be a text string describing the error;
/on_search (NACK response)
"response":
{
  "context":
  {
    "domain":"ONDC:RET10",
    "country":"IND",
    "city":"*",
    "action":"on_search",

/select
Scenarios
for both scenarios below:
   * if there is a change in delivery address, BNP is required to call /select again;
   * if there is a change in cart in /on_init (i.e. due to reduction in item quantity), BNP is required to call /select again;
1. Buyer creates make-to-order product - Domino’s Pizza (example 1 above)
In this example:
   * Buyer selects the following:
   * Dynamic Item 1 (DI1):
   * Farmhouse Pizza with Crust ("New Hand Tossed") - ₹269
   * Size ("Large") - ₹450
   * Toppings
   * "Grilled Mushrooms" - ₹80
   * "Pepper Barbeque Chicken" - ₹95
   * Dynamic Item 2 (DI2):
   * Farmhouse Pizza with Crust ("100% Wheat Thin Crust") - ₹269
   * Size ("Large") - ₹450
   * Toppings
   * "Grilled Mushrooms" - ₹80
   * "Fresh Tomato" - ₹80
   * Base item & all customizations, for a selection, are grouped using a dynamic item id;

________________
/on_select
   * SNP is required to perform check for serviceability & inventory, for the /select request, and return appropriate response as shown below;
   * order quote should comply with the following:
   * all product prices (title_type "item") should have both total & unit prices;
   * precision for all prices in quote can be up to 2 decimals;
   * order value, i.e. quote.price.value = Σ quote.breakup[].price.value;
   * total price for an item should match the unit price for the item * quantity for the item in the quote;
   * quote provided here is not frozen until /on_init;

N.B.
   1. For customizations, the above quote structure will also be a part of the payloads in /on_init, /on_confirm, /on_update, /on_cancel;
   2. In case a customization is out-of-stock, the quantity should be 0 and the total price for the customization will be 0;
   3. If any mandatory customization is out-of-stock or the required minimum quantity is not available, the BNP may prompt the buyer to select a different customization (for the same customization group and matching the veg/non-veg/egg type of the original customization selected by buyer);
   4. If any optional customization is out-of-stock or the quantity selected is not available, the quote should have the customization with the quantity available, but the base item and other customizations will have the quantity as selected by the buyer;
   5. If there is a mismatch between the list of ids in error.message & the ids in quote (with quantity less than requested) or error.message format isn’t honoured, BNP may NACK /on_select with error code 22507;

Rules for order confirmation
   * /confirm and /on_confirm calls are idempotent;
   * BNP creates the order id which will be unique across the network;
   * in response to /confirm from BNP, SNP sends /on_confirm with the same order_id;
   * BNP sends /confirm, SNP validates[629] order:
   * validation successful, SNP responds with ACK:
   * SNP creates order (preferably with internal state to indicate order is being processed), but should not forward to merchant for processing & fulfillment;
   * validation not successful, SNP responds with NACK with error code 31002 (order validation failure):
   * after BNP receives NACK, they should cancel the order with reason code 999 (order cancelled because of order confirmation failure);
   * if this order is passed in subsequent API calls (/confirm, /status, /cancel, /update, etc.), SNP returns NACK with error code 30018 (order not found);
   * SNP may also respond with NACK due to other internal errors (http 504, retriable error code 31001):
   * BNP should retry[630] /confirm:
   * if after the retry interval, BNP doesn’t receive ACK/NACK, they should cancel the order with reason code 999;
   * if BNP doesn’t receive ACK/NACK or /on_confirm, they should retry /confirm (same as above).
   * if within retry interval, BNP doesn’t receive ACK/NACK or /on_confirm, they should cancel the order with reason code 999;
   * SNP sends /on_confirm, BNP validates[631] order:
   * validation successful, BNP responds with ACK:
   * SNP forwards order to merchant for processing & fulfillment;
   * validation not successful, BNP responds with NACK with error code 23002 (order validation failure):
   * after SNP receives NACK, they should cancel the order with reason code 998 (order cancelled because of order confirmation failure) & push the status change to BNP;
   * if this order (with cancellation state & reason code) is passed in subsequent API calls (/on_confirm, /on_status, /on_cancel, /on_update), BNP responds with ACK;
   * BNP may also NACK due to internal errors (http 504/503, retriable error code 23001):
   * SNP should retry[632] /on_confirm. If after the retry interval, SNP doesn’t receive ACK/NACK, they should cancel the order with reason code 998;
   * if order is passed in subsequent API calls within the retry window (/status, /track, /cancel, /update), SNP responds with current order state along with error code 31003 to indicate order processing in progress;
   * if order is passed in subsequent API calls after cancellation (/status, /cancel, /update), SNP sends response with order state as cancelled;
   * if SNP doesn’t receive ACK/NACK for /on_confirm, they should retry /on_confirm:
   * if after the retry interval, SNP doesn’t receive ACK/NACK, they should cancel the order with reason code 998;
Return
Scenario 1 - Part cancel by merchant
   * Cancel of item(s) can only be initiated if fulfillment state is "Pending";
   * Separate fulfillment is created for the cancellation and the item & quantity assigned to it; this fulfillment also has associated details such as cancellation reason code, quote trail;
   * For part cancel of dynamic item for specific quantity:
   * the base item and customizations should be cancelled in the same proportion and the quote updated accordingly, i.e. SNP cancels the dynamic item and sets the quantity & total price to 0 for all item & customization components;
   * individual item or customization components can’t be part-cancelled;
   * if either of the above is not followed, BNP should NACK the /on_update with error code 22508;
   * For merchant part-cancel:
   * BNP may send NACK with error code 22501 (if the buyer does not accept part fill for the order);
   * In this case, the SNP will be required to rollback this part cancel request and cancel the full order;
   * Updated quote is provided by the SNP at the refund trigger state ("Liquidated", "Return_Picked", "Cancelled") and the BNP can calculate the amount of refund from the quote trail;

Scenario 2 - Return with liquidation
   * Return of items can only be initiated:
   * within the return window for the item (as defined in the catalog);
   * when fulfillment state, corresponding to item, is "Order-delivered";
   * Return with liquidation can transition through either of the following state changes:
   * Scenario A - Return liquidated:
   * Return_Initiated -> Liquidated (refund triggered here)
   * Scenario B - Return rejected:
   * Return_Initiated -> Return_Rejected
   * If return reason code is invalid, SNP can NACK /update, with error code 30005;

________________
Rules for return
   1. Order may be updated, at its terminal state ("Completed"), for the following:
   1. with order.state = "Completed", there may be return of 1 or more items, within the return window for these items:
   1. For every return request, a separate fulfillment is created to track the return request and the refund associated with the return request;
   2. Response for part-return should have exactly the same number of items for which return is requested;
   3. Order value (quote.price.value) cannot increase through /on_update:
   1. if order value decreases, it should be due to decrease in item quantity (quote.breakup[]."@ondc/org/item_quantity".count) for "@ondc/org/title_type" of "item";
   2. quote trail is immutable, after it is added to the order at the refund trigger point;
   4. /on_update (solicited or unsolicited) should be called:
   1. whenever there is change in the order details (e.g. due to buyer return);
   1. whenever there is only a status change, an unsolicited /on_status call should be made;
   2. /on_update should return the same information as /on_status i.e. the audit trail for items (including returns, cancels processed or in-progress), the current state of order items & fulfillment, order quote and breakup, settlement trail (if available);
   5. Batching of order updates & status changes should not be done;
________________
Cancellation
/cancel
      * If cancellation_reason_id is invalid (i.e. doesn’t exist or isn’t applicable for BNP), SNP can NACK /cancel with error code 30012;
      * Cancellation can be initiated by BNP on fulfillment TAT breach with cancellation_reason_id "006" and with the appropriate fulfillment id as shown:
      * if SNP determines that fulfillment TAT is not breached, they can NACK /cancel with error code 30014;
      * Force cancellation flow here;

/on_cancel
      * SNP can initiate cancellation of order using /on_cancel by setting order state & all fulfillment states to "Cancelled";[s]
      * SNP can cancel fulfillment using /on_cancel by setting corresponding fulfillment state to "Cancelled";
      * if cancellation_reason_id is not valid for unsolicited /on_cancel (i.e. not one of the cancellation reasons that can be used by SNP), BNP may NACK /on_cancel with error code 22502;
      * if updated quote does not match the original order value with the cancellation terms applied, BNP may NACK /on_cancel with error code 22503;

/on_cancel (RTO flow)
      * RTO will be initiated at the fulfillment level due to either of the following:
      * buyer does not accept the fulfillment;
      * buyer cannot be located for their fulfillment to be delivered;
      * SNP (or LSP) inability to deliver because of natural calamities, vehicle breakdown, etc.;
      * buyers are within their rights to RTO, if the fulfillment is delivered beyond the fulfillment TAT, thus constituting a TAT breach:
      * in event of RTO, without breach of fulfillment TAT, LBNP may recover both the forward shipping cost as well as RTO costs from the BNP;
      * RTO process flow for logistics is here;

Tracking
      * Tracking should be available for the fulfillment, for the order, and becomes active after rider is assigned, and inactive after the order is delivered;
      * Tracking can be based on gps coordinates or URL:
      * for gps coordinate tracking, SNP needs to set "gps_enabled" to "yes", for the corresponding fulfillment, in /on_status;
      * BNP will need to call /track to poll near real-time gps coordinates for the rider;
      * /on_track will be solicited response as explained above;
      * for URL tracking, SNP should set "url_enabled" to "yes" and "tracking_url", for the corresponding fulfillment, in /on_status;
      * If /track is called for an order for which the rider is not yet assigned or rider is assigned but fulfillment tracking is not yet enabled (i.e. "gps_enabled" and / or "url_enabled" is "no") or disabled, the SNP must return NACK with error code 40005;
      * for on-network logistics, /track request & /on_track response are cascaded from SNP to LSP & back;

/on_status
      * /on_status response can be solicited or unsolicited;
      * /on_status returns the audit trail for order items (including status of item returns, cancels processed or in-progress), the current state of order items & fulfillments, order quote & breakup:
      * SNP maintains a copy of the order, which includes the order at /on_confirm and an audit trail of all post-order flow processes;
      * same order will be returned in any post-order flow callback, such as /on_status, /on_update, /on_cancel;
      * sample payload below shows order state for normal order and doesn’t include post-order flow processes such as cancel, return, etc;
      * BNP may send NACK for /on_status with error code for cases such as:
      * NACK received by seller app for /on_confirm but seller app sends /on_status to update order state to "Accepted";
      * In case of NACK received for /on_status, SNP should rollback order to previous state of the order, i.e. the state prior to sending /on_status;

Feature discovery - 000
      * Dynamic mechanism for BNP & SNP[w][x] to mutually discover the features supported:
      * All features supported by the protocol will be documented as part of the API contract;
      * Features will be of 2 types:
      * "Baseline" - to be supported by all NPs;
      * "Enhanced" - NPs may prioritize & enable specific features, as per their business requirements;
      * BNP will communicate the list of "enhanced" features that are supported, as part of (full catalog) /search;
      * SNP will need to maintain the list of features supported by each BNP, so that order & post-order flows for a specific BNP can complete successfully;
      * In case SNP sends payload for a function not supported by a BNP, BNP can NACK the response with error code 21001;
      * New features will mostly start as "enhanced", but may move to "baseline" in a future version;
      * With every change in the "baseline" list, context.core_version will be updated;
      * List of features is here;

Other baseline features - 000
Other baseline features include:
      * Catalog taxonomy changes:
      * Grocery (RET10)
      * Sub-category Cleaning & Household to be removed;
      * New sub-categories - "Detergents and Dishwash" (for detergent bars / powders / liquids, dishwash bars / powders / liquids / paste, fabric pre & post wash);
      * Fashion (RET12)
      * New catalog attribute - "style_code", to be provided by brands & will be unique descriptor for branded product;
      * New sub-categories - "Stoles & Scarves", "Mufflers";
      * Appliances (RET15)
      * Following sub-categories moved to BPC (RET13):
      * "Trimmer"
      * "Shaver"
      * "Epilator"
      * "Hair Straightener"
      * "Hair Dryer"
      * "Hair Curler"
      * "Hair Crimper"
      * Home & Kitchen (RET16)
      * Sub-category "Cleaning Supplies" to be removed;
      * New sub-categories:
      * "Bins and Bathroom" - for disinfectant sprays & cleaners, buckets & mugs, dustbin, hangers, clips & rope, plasticware, soap cases & dispensers, toilet cleaner, floor cleaner;
      * "Car and Shoe Care" - for car polish & cleaners, shoe polish, shoe shiners & brushes;
      * "Disposables and Garbage Bags" - for kitchen rolls, paper napkins, wet wipes, toilet paper;
      * "Fresheners and Repellents" - for air freshener, insect repellant, mosquito repellant;
      * "Mops, Brushes and Scrubs" - for brooms & dust pans, dust & cloth wipes, mops, utensils scrub pad, glove, toilet & other brushes;
      * "Party and Festive Needs" - for caps, balloons & candles, decorations, disposable cups and plates, gifts, gift wraps & bags;
      * "Flowers" - for fresh flowers, artificial flowers;
      * "Pooja Needs" - for agarbatti, incense sticks, camphors & wicks, lamp & lamp oils, candles & matchbox, pooja thalis, other pooja needs;
      * Rating:
      * As part of the catalog, fetch rating for provider, items;

Self-pickup - 002
      * Provider will define whether their store supports delivery, self-pickup or both options, along with the timings for delivery, self-pickup;
      * SNP will forward delivery (only if pickup & delivery locations serviceable), self-pickup option for buyer to select:
      * delivery option will have an O2D TAT while self-pickup option will have the O2S TAT;
      * delivery will be the 1st fulfillment option, (with the SNP assigning this delivery option for the items), but the quote will include the cost for both delivery & self-pickup types (including "delivery", "packing", "tax" (with quote type "fulfillment"), as applicable);
      * BNP should check the default fulfillment(s) assigned to item(s) and extract the cost only for these fulfillment(s), from the quote, for displaying to the buyer along with other line items such as item, tax, etc;
      * Buyer may change the fulfillment option to self-pickup and this will be updated in /init:
      * when the buyer selects a fulfillment option, among options provided by the SNP, the selected fulfillment option will be communicated in /init. In this case, the selected fulfillment option will impact the quote and the quote in /on_init may be different from the quote in /on_select;
      * BNP will need to validate that the updated quote in /on_init matches the quote in /on_select after adjusting for the changes in quote due to the fulfillment option selected e.g. if /on_select quote included a value for delivery charge and this was the default fulfillment option and the buyer selects self-pickup, the updated quote should have a delivery charge of 0 in /on_init;
      * If cart selection changes (i.e. change in items and / or quantity), BNP needs to call /select;
      * SNP should check that the quote in /confirm matches the last quote sent in /on_init;
      * In case of self-pickup:
      * after the order is packed, it is ready for pickup by seller;
      * pickup code will be generated by SNP and communicated to BNP;
      * authorization code (OTP, etc.) may optionally be generated by SNP and communicated to BNP;
      * additional details that may be required to be communicated over the protocol include vehicle no. for curbside self-pickup;
      * instructions if any (e.g. with register / counter no for buyer self-pickup);

Slotted delivery - 003
      * BNP may show buyer available delivery slots for fulfillment (/on_select):
      * NP providing fulfillment may maintain inventory of all fulfillment slots;
      * SNP, providing fulfillment, can communicate available delivery slot(s) for buyer to select:
      * each delivery slot will be for an unique fulfillment;
      * BNP, providing fulfillment, can show available delivery slots to buyer but only communicate the selected delivery slot to SNP;
      * BNP communicates selected delivery slot to SNP (/init);

Fulfillment by BNP - 004
      * Logistics fulfillment by BNP will be based on the logistics API contract;
      * Since logistics is a separate domain, BNP needs to register as LBNP;
      * Since SNP may support BNP fulfillment for all or specific items, they need to enable the fulfillment type "Buyer-Delivery", for items for which this is supported;
      1. Pre-order flow
      * LBNP sends /search to gateway & gateway broadcasts to LSPs:
      * Logistics /search requires start & end gps coordinates & city code, weight / dimensions of package being shipped, etc.;
      * LSP(s) send logistics catalog directly to LBNP;
      * Logistics /search may be sequenced after receiving response for retail /select;
      * BNP may also maintain local rate card for logistics, which includes rate, TAT for distance slabs;
      * If SNP supports "Buyer-Delivery" fulfillment type, /on_select should have for the corresponding fulfillment:
      * delivery charge of 0, for this fulfillment;
      * quote with packaging charges / convenience fee, as applicable;
      * O2S TAT;
      * for fulfillment options from LSP, BNP will need to compute O2D as O2S + S2D (S2D will have 1st mile & last mile components and there may be an overlap between O2S & 1st mile component especially for F&B);
      * weight & dimensions of package;
      * SNP may also include their own fulfillment types (for delivery, self-pickup);
      * BNP consolidates fulfillment options from LSP & SNP for buyer;
      * If buyer selects fulfillment corresponding to "Buyer-Delivery" fulfillment type, corresponding fulfillment id should be mapped to item and passed in /init to SNP along with the customer’s contact number:
      * In response, SNP will send the updated quote, for the selected fulfillment, including packaging charges / convenience fee (as applicable) & O2S TAT;
      * SNP also updates whether RTO action should result in actual return to origin;
      * Order will be confirmed with SNP with the above fulfillment id / quote / TAT as sent by SNP in /on_init along with the customer’s name and contact number; 
      * Logistics order will be confirmed by LBNP with the fulfillment id selected above;

      2. Post-order flow
Status update
      * SNP updates retail order state to "Packed";
      * SNP notifies "ready_to_ship" for retail order:
      * "ready_to_ship" and "Packed" may be sent in any sequence:
      * at the same time;
      * "ready_to_ship" followed by "Packed";
      * "Packed" followed by "ready_to_ship";
      * SNP may provide pickup instructions for rider;
      * On receiving "ready_to_ship" from SNP, LBNP notifies "ready_to_ship" to LSP, with pickup code & merchant order reference no:
      * In response, LSP updates pickup slot & shipping label for hub-based delivery only;
      * BNP forwards pickup slot & shipping label (for hub-based delivery) to SNP using /update;
      * When agent is assigned ("Agent-assigned"), LSP sends agent details to LBNP using /on_status:
      * BNP forwards this status to SNP using /update:
      * SNP will need to handle cases where fulfillment states are received out of sequence, e.g. "Agent-assigned" before "Packed";
      * Update of fulfillment states from pickup to delivery:
      * After fulfillment is picked up, LSP updates status of logistics order to "Order-picked-up", with pickup time:
      * BNP requests update of retail order / fulfillment state & pickup time using /update;
      * After fulfillment is delivered, LSP updates state of logistics order to "Order-delivered":
      * BNP requests update of retail order / fulfillment state & delivery time using /update;
      * All interim states to be updated the same way;
      * After all fulfillments are marked "Order-delivered", SNP should update order state to "Completed";

Cancellation
LSP cancels
      * LSP cancels logistics order using /on_cancel, with appropriate reason code and subscriber id in "cancelled_by";
      * BNP initiates cancellation of retail order / fulfillment, cascading the cancellation reason from LSP;
      * BNP requests state update, for forward & RTO fulfillment, as applicable for retail order (see "update_state" above);
      * Cancellation charges, if any, will be communicated by BNP to SNP, if SNP is liable for such charges:
      * state update & cancellation charges will be communicated to SNP using /update, before order reaches terminal state;
      * cancellation charges will not be included in the order quote and separate keys will be provided for this (as these are receivables due from SNP to BNP);
BNP cancels
      * BNP cancels retail order / fulfillment using /cancel;
      * BNP cancels logistics order using /cancel;
      * BNP requests state update, for forward & RTO fulfillment, for retail order (see "update_state" above);
      * Cancellation charges, if any, will be communicated by BNP to SNP, if SNP is liable for such charges:
      * state update & cancellation charges will be communicated to SNP using /update;
      * cancellation charges will not be included in the order quote and separate keys will be provided for this (as these are receivables due from SNP to BNP);
SNP cancels
      * SNP cancels retail order / fulfillment using /on_cancel;
      * BNP cancels logistics order, cancelling the cascaded reason from SNP;
      * BNP request state update, for forward & RTO fulfillment, for retail order (see "update_state" above);
      * Cancellation charges, if any, will be communicated by BNP to SNP, if SNP is liable for such charges:
      * state update & cancellation charges will be communicated to SNP using /update;
      * cancellation charges will not be included in the order quote and separate keys will be provided for this (as these are receivables due from SNP to BNP);

________________
Return
Scenarios
      * SNP handles return pickup:
      * existing scenario applies, no payload changes;
      * no additional charges to be sent in order quote;
      * SNP doesn’t handle return pickup:
      * BNP sends return request (same as for above scenario);
      * SNP approves return request with state "Return_Approved":
      * SNP also includes reverse qc input for return pickup check;
      * BNP creates order for logistics for return pickup;
      * BNP requests update for fulfillment state, reverse qc output for return fulfillment (see "Status update" above);
      * BNP will need to factor in return costs;

Tracking
      * Tracking of order / fulfillment will be directly between BNP & LSP:
      * Tracking by SNP may be enabled later;
Weight differential charges
      * LSP sends updated quote / weight / dimension due to weight differential to LBNP (BNP):
      * BNP forwards weight / dimension differentials, receivables due from SNP;
      * Resolution of weight differential charges:
      * SNP to inform BNP if they accept or dispute the weight differential updates:
      * If SNP disputes:
      * SNP may use error code 41002 to indicate non-acceptance;
      * LBNP may communicate to LSP that weight differential charges are rejected;
      * LSP handles order delivery as per agreed terms;
      * resolution of dispute will follow IGM route;
      * If SNP accepts:
      * differential cost will not be included in order quote and separate attribute keys will be provided for this (as these are receivables due from SNP to BNP);

Force cancellation - 005
      1. Considering that /cancel is a request by BNP for SNP to cancel order / fulfillment, there may be a need for BNP to initiate "force cancellation" for certain cases like buyer requesting cancellation due to fulfillment TAT breach;
      2. Cancellation terms may be defined by SNP:
      1. includes cancellation fee as flat amount / % (% to be interpreted as follows):
      1. % of order value (excluding taxes) for order cancellation;
      2. % of fulfillment value (i.e. item + fulfillment level costs excluding taxes) for fulfillment cancellation (in case of multiple fulfillments);
      3. for order with multiple fulfillments, cancellation fees may be defined as %;
      2. can be optionally defined at:
      1. order level (in /on_init);
      3. will be applicable, for cancellation of order / fulfillment, only after corresponding order state is "Accepted";
      3. Cancellation terms definition:
      1. /on_init - cancellation fee for specific fulfillment state & reason code, with option for wildcard ("*") as the catch-all clause covering combination of fulfillment state & reason code not specifically defined;
      4. Cancellation fee calculation:
      1. for /on_cancel response:
      1. (order value - updated order value in /on_cancel)
      2. for no /on_cancel response:
      1. if matching the specific fulfillment state & reason code, the cancellation fee will be as defined in cancellation terms for /on_init;
      2. if not matching, cancellation fee will be 0;
      5. Cancellation:
      1. BNP initiates cancellation for order / fulfillment using /cancel (with reason code / fulfilment id, as applicable);
      2. Includes TAT for receiving valid cancellation response;
      3. If SNP sends valid /on_cancel response within TAT:
      1. response has updated quote, order / fulfillment state set to cancelled;
      2. BNP processes response and calculates cancellation fee as defined above;
      4. If SNP doesn’t send valid response / doesn’t respond within TAT:
      1. BNP sends force cancel request for order / fulfillment, i.e. /cancel request with "force" = "yes";
      2. If SNP sends valid response within TAT, processing will be as defined in c above;
      3. If SNP doesn’t send (valid) response:
      * BNP will create IGM issue for resolution (after expiry of TAT), including details such as cancellation fee calculated, refund issued (as applicable);
      * resolution of IGM issue will create a valid /on_cancel response for the "force" cancellation;
      * BNP will refund the order amount to the buyer and no settlement will be processed with SNP[ad][ae][af];
      * In case of a disagreement regarding the settlement process, SNP will raise an IGM issue for resolution;[ag]
      6. IGM Handling:

To handle disagreements in the settlement/reconciliation process, the SNP can initiate an IGM (v2.0) request to the buyer app with the issue category set to "PAYMENT" or "TECHNICAL", as enumerated here.

Return with pickup - 006
         * Return of items can only be initiated, within the return window for the item (as defined in the catalog), when fulfillment state for item is "Order-delivered";
         * Return, with pickup, can have following scenarios:
         * Scenario A - Return approved, Return pick successful:
         * Return_Initiated -> Return_Approved -> Return_Picked (refund triggered here) -> Return_Delivered
         * Return_Initiated -> Return_Approved -> Return_Pick_Failed -> Return_Picked (refund triggered here) -> Return_Delivered
         * Scenario B - Return approved, Return failed:
         * Return_Initiated -> Return_Approved -> Return_Pick_Failed -> Return_Failed
         * Scenario C - Return rejected:
         * Return_Initiated -> Return_Rejected
         * It is assumed that the LSP assigned for return pickup will have a certain no of pickup attempts and will trigger scenario B after all pickup attempts failed;
         3. Buyer initiates return request (item i1, qty 1)

SNP collecting payment - 007
         1. SNP that wants to collect payment should set "bpp_terms"."collect_payment" to "Y" in /on_search (full catalog refresh);
         2. BNP that wants to place order with this SNP will need to render the payment link sent by SNP:
         1. SNP sends following additional attributes in /on_init for rendering payment link:
         1. payment.type="ON-ORDER" (prepaid);
         2. payment.collected_by="BPP";
         3. payment.uri="secure_public_pg_link";
         4. payment.status="NOT-PAID";
         2. BNP will need to render this payment link for the buyer, after receiving the /on_init response;
         3. SNP updates payment collection details using unsolicited /on_init:
         1. Scenario 1 - collection successful, payment status updated:
         1. payment.params:currency, amount (order value), transaction_id (UTR);
         2. payment.status="PAID";
         3. payment.tags.bpp_collect.success="Y";
         4. in this case, BNP should proceed with /confirm;
         2. Scenario 2 - collection successful, payment status not updated:
         1. payment.params:currency, amount (order value), transaction_id (if available);
         2. payment.status="NOT-PAID";
         3. payment.tags.bpp_collect.success="Y";
         4. in this case, BNP may terminate the transaction or proceed with /confirm. If BNP proceeds with /confirm, SNP should honour /confirm as per the contract and it will be the SNP’s responsibility to subsequently update payment.status when available;
         3. Scenario 3 - collection error:
         1. payment.params:currency, amount (order value);
         2. payment.status="NOT-PAID";
         3. payment.tags.bpp_collect.success="N";
         4. payment.tags.bpp_collect.error="error_message";
         5. in this case, BNP should terminate the transaction;
         4. If BNP doesn’t receive payment collection details (as per 3 above) within its TAT:
         1. BNP should terminate the transaction and if the payment collection details are subsequently received, it should NACK /on_init with error code 20009;
         2. BNP may also send another /init request for the latest payment collection details and follow (a) above if the /on_init callback doesn’t have the required payment collection details;

Minimum order value - 008
         * SNP may specify minimum order value per store;
         * If cart value is less than minimum order value during checkout (/select, /init), SNP can return error code 30023 in callback response, and BNP may use this to prompt the buyer to increase the order value to be above the minimum order value;

Offers
         * Offer construct - includes:
         * applicability criteria - defines where / when / on what offer(s) may be applicable:
         * location(s);
         * categories;
         * item(s);
         * time period validity;
         * applicability criteria, for an offer, will be:
         * intersection of the defined attributes, i.e. location(s) and categories and time period validity, if these are the attributes defined for the offer;[ah][ai][aj][ak]
         * within a multi-valued attribute, applicability criteria will apply to union of all values, e.g. for location L1 & L2, offer applies to L1 or L2;
         * qualifier - qualifying / eligibility criteria;
         * benefit - benefit to the buyer from the offer(s);
         * meta info - other info, i.e. whether offer requires explicit buyer opt-in, whether an offer can be applied in addition to other offer(s);
         * other info - includes offer id / type, images, etc;
         * Offer flows:
         * Publish offer - SNP publishes offers, per provider, in the full and/or incremental catalog refresh:
         * BNP may display one or more of these offers on their app, to enable buyer discovery;
         * Offer definition is templatized below and the BNP can create an appropriate description for an offer from the template variables (qualifier, benefit) and using the applicability criteria as defined above;
         * Apply offer - SNP applies offer(s) to the order quote, during the buyer checkout flow:
         * SNP may apply offer(s), without publishing, in the full or incremental catalog refresh;
         * Offer is applied as part of processing request (/select, /init):
         * SNP evaluates offers for which buyer is eligible, regardless of applicability of such offers, and sends details of these offers in /on_select;
         * SNP validates offer id(s), for opt-in offers, and applies the offer(s) to the cart selection;
         * offers based on buyer identification can be applied while processing /init;
         * auto-applied offers will be shown in the offer quote. If buyer doesn’t want any auto-applied offer, they can remove the offer from the cart and BNP will communicate this to SNP in the subsequent request (/select, /init);
         * Offers, resulting in monetary benefit to buyer, will be applied to the order quote:
         * Cart level offers, will be applied at the "order" level in the quote, and the attributes in "benefit" below will be a part of the "offer" quote line item;
         * allocation of order level offers, to individual line items, is at the discretion of the BNPs, subject to:
         * absolute aggregate of the offer reversal values cannot exceed the offer values applied at the time of order creation;
         * Any reversal of offer value, due to cancellation / return, etc. will have to be explicitly defined in quote_trail;
         * Reverse offer - whenever an offer qualifier is no longer valid in the post-order flow, SNP may decide to reverse the offer, in part or full, up to the benefit provided to the buyer, in aggregate;
         * Exception conditions for offers:
         * if offer is no longer valid in pre-order APIs such as /on_init or /on_confirm, SNP can send error code 30006;
         * if offer is valid but cannot be fulfilled, e.g. offer item not available for offers such as freebie, etc., SNP can send error code 30007;
         * if offer is no longer valid or cannot be fulfilled in /on_confirm, SNP should cancel the order;
         * Offer template - in the template below (M - mandatory, O - optional, N/A - not applicable):

	         * offer type:
         * discount - discount percent or amount applied to the cart value, with or without a cap, and may be based on minimum cart value;
         * buyXgetY - for every "X" item count in the cart, total of "Y" items will be offered (i.e. "Y" - "X" additional items), at offered value;
         * freebie - for a minimum order value, 1 or more free item(s) will be offered at 0 value;
         * slab - distinct slabs for applicable discount for range of item quantity; 
         * combo - discount for (primary) item and 1 or more (secondary) items;
         * delivery - discount on delivery charges, with or without a cap;
         * exchange - 1 or more catalog items can be purchased in lieu of an existing item owned by the buyer;
         * financing - SNP financing available for 1 or more catalog items;
         * qualifier:
         * min value - min cart value for the offer to be applicable, i.e. aggregate value of all items in cart, not including taxes, delivery & packaging charges;
         * item count - min count of items in the cart for the offer to be applicable;
         * item count upper - max count of items in the cart for the offer to be applicable;
         * item id - (secondary) item(s) for the offer;
         * benefit:
         * value - discount on the cart value (-ve) offered;
         * value type - "percent", "amount";
         * value cap - cap on the offer value;
         * item count - additional count of items offered;
         * item id - additional item offered, should be part of the catalog;
         * item value - offered value of item;
         * meta:
         * additive - whether offer can be applied with other offers;
         * auto - whether offer is auto-applied or requires explicit opt-in by buyer;

Reverse offer[bo][bp][bq]

Purchase finance by BNP - 0099
            * Proposed flow for on-network purchase finance by BNP, also as the loan buyer app:
            * SNP provides consent for financing, of specific items, by tagging the corresponding items in the offers applicability criteria:
            * SNP provides maximum subvention % (pegged to the price of the product) they’re willing to pay to the lender;
            * Loan buyer app provides financing options to buyer, before confirmation of retail order:
            * SNP sends account details,[ci][cj][ck] PAN no which are forwarded to loan provider for completion of loan transaction;
            * after completion of loan transaction, BNP sends following info to SNP: loan completed ("yes" / "no"), following details for loan completed "yes":
            * down payment
            * loan amount
            * loan provider
            * Loan sanction ID (Down payment ID)
            * UTR no for confirmation of remittance completed to the seller's bank account;
            * effective subvention
            * timestamp
            * retail order will record the buyer as having collected the full payment, e.g: if retail order value is ₹10K, with down payment of ₹1K & loan amount of ₹9K, retail order will record value as ₹10K;
            * for reverse transactions like cancellation, retail buyer app informs loan provider & seller and loan provider / retail buyer app credits the down payment to buyer;
            * item verification attributes (e.g. IMEI no) may be provided in /on_status, at or after fulfillment state of "Order-picked-up", for the forward shipment;

Commercial Model for BNP/SNP - 00A[cy][cz]
            * Buyer Finder Fee (BFF) in /search becomes optional, to ensure backward compatibility;
            * SNP communicates the following as part of full catalog refresh (/on_search):
            * channel margin at provider / category / item level;
            * channel margin at item level overrides value at category level, which overrides value at provider level;
            * Handling of possible scenarios:
            * BNP sends BFF in full catalog refresh (/search):
            * SNP responds with their commercial model (channel margin) => SNP commercial model overrides BNP BFF;
            * SNP doesn’t respond with their commercial model => BNP BFF applies;
            * BNP doesn’t send BFF in full catalog /search:
            * SNP responds with their commercial model (channel margin) => SNP commercial model applies;
            * SNP doesn’t respond with their commercial model => channel margin to be considered as 0;
            * SNP applies channel margin (at item level) and sends as part of quote (/on_select):
            * Channel margin, at item level, can override values at category and provider level, specified in full catalog refresh;
            * Channel margin applied using the convenience fee quote line item type (title_type="misc");
            * If there are multiple options for channel margin, there will be separate quote line items for each such option;
            * BNP selects a specific option for each item and sends as part of /init;
            * In response, SNP sends the updated quote (including the quote line item for selected option) in /on_init;
            * For COD payment collection, where seller (SNP) is delivering the order, BNP communicates to the SNP the platform fees, if any, to be collected;
Payload changes

Replacement flow - 00B
            * Replacement flow:
            * SNP defines replacement terms in their catalog - whether replacement allowed, replacement window;
            * Buyer decides return / replacement for specific item(s);
            * BNP sends replacement request to SNP;
            * SNP initiates return fulfillment and arranges for pickup of item(s) from buyer;
            * On return pickup, SNP initiates forward fulfillment for replacement item(s);
Payload changes
            1. /on_search - catalog with replacement terms

  }

Exchange flow - 00C
            * Proposed flow for deferred exchange:
            * Available exchange offers will be published by provider as part of their catalog, and will be visible to the buyer, through offers discovery on the Product listing page;
            * Buyer raises (deferred) exchange request, i.e. after receiving delivery of item on which exchange offer is available;
            * Exchange flow will be exactly the same as return with pickup flow, with some changes to the exchange request (/update) shown below;
            * Flow for instant exchange will be added in future;

Update delivery auth - 010
Delivery verification modes include:
            * static OTP - static for the order, without any time validity;
            * dynamic OTP - with time validity;
Proposed flow for verification
Only applies if SNP is LBNP:
            * LBNP creates verification code, for delivery:
            * LBNP sends OTP to BNP (/on_confirm) & to LSP (/confirm);
            * LSP should not forward OTP to rider as this will be provided by end buyer for verification at delivery;
            * Delivery verification:
            * Buyer provides delivery OTP at the time of order delivery;
            * Rider updates fulfillment state to "Order-delivered", with delivery OTP in /on_status, for verification by LSP;
            * Verification flow for logistics is here;

Cash on delivery (COD) order - 012
            * Since payment for COD order is on fulfillment, the NP providing fulfillment will also be the payment collector;
            * COD order requires:
            * all items in the cart to be available on COD;
            * when multiple modes of payment are made available on the payment UX (e.g. prepaid, COD), the buyer gets to choose the payment mode for the order;
            * Once the payment mode is finalized, it is communicated over the protocol;
            * For multi-fulfillment order, payment initiator, providing the UX, may decide whether to allow COD order;
            * if COD order is allowed:
            * for multi-fulfillment order, retail NP handling fulfillment may decide when to collect payment for order;[dk][dl]
            * After payment collection for the full order, retail NP handling fulfillment updates payment status for the order;
            * Settlement will be initiated by the payment collector;
            * On-network logistics COD order is documented here;

Order price adjustment not tied to return or cancel - 013
            * Order price adjustment (post-confirmation), not tied to return or cancellation:
            * will be in the form of price reduction, for 1 or more items, in the order;
            * can be unsolicited, in the form of "quote_update" fulfillment, with quote_trail having breakup of delta changes in price, with updated quote; this fulfillment will also be linked to the forward fulfillment(s) of the items for which delta price change has been applied;
            * can be applied before order reaches terminal state of "Completed" or "Cancelled";
            * in some cases, due to issue / dispute resolution, order price adjustment may be required after terminal state of "Completed":
            * in such cases, IGM issue id must also be provided thru "id" in "igm_request";

Cross-category order flow - 014[dm]
            * Cross-category single-cart order, for a specific provider, can be created as follows:
            * Specific provider, for an SNP, is identified by the same unique identifier (bpp/providers[].id), across catalogs for different RET domains;
            * SNP assigns the same unique identifier to the provider and unique identifier for items across RET domains for the provider;
            * BNP can allow cart creation using multiple items, for same provider, across the different RET domains;
            * Order flow, for specific provider, can include items from catalogs in multiple RET domains, e.g. single cart creation for grocery (RET10), BPC (RET13), H&W (RET18) items from the same provider, with 1 or more fulfillment(s);
            * Cross-RET domain for order flow can be identified using Context.domain="ONDC:FFFFF[1163]", in all APIs except /search and /on_search;
            * BFF for the order is calculated as shown below;
            * Signing of the API request / response will use the private signing keys of the NP for any of the [dn][do]RET domains;
BFF calculation
Scenario[dp][dq][dr][ds]
            1. 3 items in cart:
            1. I1 (qty 1) - RET10
            2. I2 (qty 1) - RET13
            3. I3 (qty 2) - RET18
            2. BFF:
            1. RET10 - 3%
            2. RET13 - 5%
            3. RET18 - 5%
            4. GST - 18%
            3. List price[1164] per qty:
            1. I1 - ₹100
            2. I2 - ₹200
            3. I3 - ₹250
            4. Delivery charge - ₹50 (excluding GST)
            5. GST:
            1. Product (I1, I2, I3) - 5%
            2. Delivery - 18%
Calculation
            1. Total item cost = ₹100*1 + ₹200*1 + ₹250*2 = ₹800;
            2. Delivery charge = ₹50;
            3. BFF calculation:
            1. Items = ₹100*0.0354[1165] + ₹200*0.059 + ₹500*0.059 = ₹44.84;
            2. Delivery (using minimum BFF across categories) = ₹50*0.0354 = ₹1.77;
            4. BFF for order:
            1. Items + Delivery = ₹44.84 + ₹1.77 = ₹46.61;
            2. as % of order value (without taxes) = ₹46.61/(800+50) = 5.48%[1166]
            5. GST calculation:
            1. Items = ₹800*0.05 = ₹40;
            2. Delivery = ₹50*0.18 = ₹9;[dt]
            6. Total order value[1167] = ₹800+₹50+₹44.84+₹1.77+₹40+₹9 = ₹945.61;

Seller Creds - 017
            * Provider can add their credentials in the catalog, using bpp/providers.creds[], as per this list;
            * Credentials can be used to tag specific sellers, e.g. social sector sellers under specific Government schemes like ODOP, woman owned business, tribal owned business, etc.;
            * Credentials can also be used to uniquely identify sellers across the network;
            * Adding creds to Order will allow identification of orders, from providers with specific credentials, for possible incentivization;
Payload changes


{

Streamline fulfillment attributes for hyperlocal - 019
            * 2 new fulfillment states to be added for hyperlocal:
            * "At-pickup" - to be set, when rider is within the perimeter of the pickup location, as defined by LSP;
            * "At-delivery" - to be set, when rider is within the perimeter of the delivery location, as defined by LSP;
            * "Out-for-delivery" fulfillment state for hyperlocal to be deprecated;

Options for multi-fulfillment orders - 01D
            * In case of multi-fulfillment orders, where the seller can provide multiple fulfillment options for 1 or more items, all possible fulfillment options for an item should be communicated to the buyer to decide which fulfillment option to select;
            * Different fulfillment options are shown in /on_select and the buyer has to select 1 fulfillment option per item or for all items, as the case may be. This fulfillment option is communicated to the seller in /init;

Cancellation terms - 01E
            * Cancellation terms may be defined by SNP during pre-order flow:
            * applies to cancellation by BNP or SNP;
            * definition is at the fulfillment level and based on the fulfillment state & reason codes and includes associated cancellation fees (if any):
            * cancellation fees, for order cancellation, will be the aggregate of cancellation fees for individual fulfillments;
            * if cancellation terms are not acceptable to BNP, they may NACK the /on_init or /on_confirm callback, with error code 27501;
            * Actual cancellation fees are reflected in the order quote & quote trail, after cancellation of fulfillment or order;
            * With cancellation terms enabled, order cancellation, at the order / fulfillment level, may be enabled for all fulfillment states, after order has been placed ("Pending") and before it is delivered ("Order-delivered");

            * source of demand e.g. ONDC buyer app / external social media or search apps that provide deep linking to SNP store page thru banner or other targets;
            * search terms used by buyers to search for specific catalog items (may or may not be available in the catalog), to facilitate better supply planning by sellers;

            * Proof of pickup & delivery (e-POD):
            * may include image of pickup / delivery at the point of pickup / delivery;
            * may include name of authorized recipient if consignee is unavailable at delivery;
            * This feature may be required for scenarios where POD is required by BNP like Purchase Finance

Transaction level contract
Overview
            1. Purpose of the transaction level contract  between the participating NPs is explained here and includes the standard terms & conditions for the network participant(s);
            2. The codified digital contract includes a set of configurable terms defined by the seller and a set of static terms which will be defined by the BNP (BNP);
            3. A reference to these static terms will be a part of every online transaction between 2 participants;
            4. Reference clauses to serve as a guide for participants to draft their static terms for the codified digital contract can be found here;
Proposed flow
            1. Static terms will be version-controlled in GitHub repo:
            1. All static terms will start with version 1.0.0 and subsequent changes will increment the version;
            2. NP creates a PR for their static terms and ONDC will merge this PR and share the link with the NP:
            1. NP forks the repository and creates a branch under the appropriate version, using the following naming convention:
            * <NP name>_role e.g. "Pincode_BNP", "Magicpin_BNP", etc.;
            2. NP merges their static terms into this branch;
            3. NP creates PR for these changes;
            2. Static terms can be published by NP on multiple channels e.g. their website, ONDC portal, etc.
            3. Communication & acceptance of static terms:
            1. Communication by BNP
            1. BNP sends the following additional info as part of /search:
            * current static terms link with version:
            * for the very 1st set of static terms, this will be a blank link;
            * new static terms link with version, if any:
            * for the very 1st static terms, this will be the link for static terms in GitHub;
            * effective date for new static terms
            2. Info in (i) above will be sent in /search for full catalog for 24 hrs, after this version of static terms is published;
            3. 24 hrs prior to expiry of effective date in (i) above, BNP resends additional info in (i) above;
            4. If BNP wants to change the effective date, they can update the effective date in (i) above and repeat (ii) & (iii) above;
            5. If BNP wants to change their static terms, they need to resubmit their PR with new version no;
            6. It is recommended that the BNP should give at least 15 days of advance notice when they are changing their static terms.
            2. Acceptance by SNP (SNP)
            1. If SNP accepts the static terms in /search above, they need to send accept="Y" in /on_search;
            2. If SNP doesn’t accept the static terms in /search above, they need to send accept="N" in /on_search;
            3. If SNP doesn’t accept the static terms for a BNP, they should stop responding with their catalog for the corresponding BNP from the effective date;
            4. If SNP doesn’t accept the static terms but continues to send their catalog, BNP may, at their discretion, choose to delist the sellers for this SNP;
            5. Static terms agreed to between the BNP & SNP will be a part of /confirm and /confirm;

[1191] fulfillment options are F2 & F3, i.e. available for delivery between 13:30 & 14:00 or between 18:30 & 19:00 (all times in UTC); 
[1192] buyer has opted for delivery between 18:30 & 19:00 UTC (fulfillment id "F3");
[1193] means 0 cancellation fees for fulfillment in this state & for this reason code;
[1194] fulfillment state;
[1195] reason code (list here);
[1196] cancellation fee, if any for this state & reason code - either percentage (of fulfillment value minus taxes, in above format between "0.00" and "100.00") or amount needs to be provided (if both provided, minimum non-zero value may be considered by BNP);
SNP can calculate based on what needs to be deducted e.g. packaging charges / convenience fee / product cost, etc;
[1197] in case of RTO where buyer is responsible, the forward & reverse shipment costs may also be deducted as cancellation fees;
[1198] means 100% of fulfillment value (includes cost of items in fulfillment, delivery cost for fulfillment), to be deducted as cancellation fees;
[1199] list of reason codes delimited by "," (above shows RTO reason codes where buyer is not available);
[1200] if cancellation terms are different from what was quoted earlier, BNP can NACK /on_confirm with error code 22505;
[1201] "max_liability" is the maximum aggregate liability expressed as multiple of the total transaction value, while the "max_liability_cap" is the maximum aggregate liability expressed in ₹, e.g:
If max_liability is set to "2", the total transaction value is ₹100, and "max_liability_cap" is not provided, it means the aggregate liability of SNP shall not be more than ₹200 (i.e. 2 multiplied by 100). If "max_liability_cap" is set as 100, and "max_liability" is not provided, it means the maximum aggregate liability will be ₹100;
If both, "max_liability_cap" and "max_liability" are provided, the maximum aggregate liability will be the lower of the two amounts, e.g. if "max_liability" is set to "2", the total transaction value is ₹100, and "max_liability_cap" is set to 100, it means the maximum aggregate liability will be ₹100 (the lower of ₹200 and ₹100);
If neither "max_liability_cap" nor "max_liability" are provided, it means the contract does not have any clause related to limitation of liability; thus, the liability is uncapped;
If "max_liability_cap" and "max_liability" are both set to 0, it means both parties agree that BNP will not bear any liability;
[1202] enum - "true", "false";
"true" - means both parties agree that in case of a dispute, both parties must resolve the dispute through arbitration;
[1203] name of city whose courts will have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes related to this contract, will only contain Indian cities which have a High Court bench;
[1204] annual rate of interest that BNP will be charged if they delay a payment to the SNP, calculated pro rata for each calendar day of delay; e.g. if the value is set as "10.00", and the amount of payment due is INR 1000, it means the BNP will pay the SNP an interest of 10.00% per annum (i.e. INR 100), calculated pro rata for each day of delay. So if the BNP delay was 50 days, the total interest payable would be INR 13.70 [calculated as 1000x(10.00/100)x(50/365)]
[1205] in case of delivery delay (or failure), delivery slot needs to be updated and the delivery delay reason code and timestamp (when recorded) may be provided here;
